p='pom.xml'; s=open(p).read()

            </plugin>""","""                <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>

            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-dependency-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>properties</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
            <!-- Load Mockito as an agent instead of relying on dynamic self-attach (deprecated in newer JDKs) -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <argLine>@{argLine} -javaagent:${org.mockito:mockito-core:jar} -Xshare:off</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>""")
s=s.replace("<java.version>25</java.version>","<java.version>25</java.version>\n        <argLine></argLine>")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
I've set up a Maven project on Spring Boot 4.1.1 (the latest stable release on Maven Central) in `/work`. `mvn test` runs 4 tests and all pass, with no warnings.

**Testing support**

`spring-boot-starter-test` (test scope) gives you everything you asked for in one dependency:
- **Assertions:** AssertJ, plus Hamcrest.
- **Mocking:** Mockito.
- **Loading the Spring context:** Spring Test and Spring Boot Test.
- **Test runner:** JUnit Jupiter.

**Project files**
- `pom.xml`:
  - Uses the Spring Boot parent and targets Java 25 (the current LTS).
  - Includes `spring-boot-starter` and `spring-boot-maven-plugin`.
  - Configures Surefire to load Mockito as a Java agent. Without this, Mockito warns on every run that the way it attaches itself will stop working in future JDKs.
- `DemoApplication`, plus a small `GreetingService` that uses a `GreetingRepository`, so the tests have something real to exercise.
- `.gitignore` for `target/` and IDE files.

**Example tests, one for each style**
- `GreetingServiceTests`: a plain Mockito unit test (`@Mock`, `@InjectMocks`) with no Spring context.
- `DemoApplicationTests`: `@SpringBootTest` checks that the context loads and that the real beans work together.
